findings.issue: RESOLVED (fixed). Local runners now have their own request timeout (default 300 s, bounds 10..=3600) and load timeout (default 600 s, bounds 10..=7200). Model load is waited out before the first decision and does not count toward the request timeout or the 90 s start budget.

REQ-SAG-0015.md:21-25 and :40-41 state the requirement. a-5:191-193 add Timeouts::with_request, and a-5:156 adds HttpRequest::with_deadline. a-5:296 and :483 (A5-26) say the 90 s budget starts at the first send, and a-5:424 tests it (budget_starts_at_first_send). a-6:215 adds wait_until_loaded(.., load_timeout, ..) and a-6:246 adds LoadTimeout (local.load_timeout). a-6:228 covers load-on-first-request per daemon kind. a-6:320-323 test polling, load timeout, cancel, and the Laya deadline of load+request. a-10:230-231 build one UreqTransport per local runner with Timeouts::default().with_request(runner.request_timeout()).

findings.issue: Introduced by the fix. The worst-case wall-clock paragraph still says 'last start's send ends within its 120 s request deadline ... finishes within 210 s'. That is true only for remote providers. For a local runner with the default 300 s timeout the worst case is about 90 s + 300 s = 390 s. For a Laya first request it is 90 s + (600 + 300) s.
findings.recommendation: Qualify line 298 as remote-only. Add the local formula: 90 s + the runner's request timeout, and 90 s + load + request for the first Laya request.
